chunk_findings.detail:
When the ceiling cannot be met by trimming, the loop only exits via the `not (n_dec or n_les)` branch, so `over=True` always implies `decisions_shown == 0` **and** `lessons_shown == 0` (the other two exit conditions require `max_chars` falsy or `len(text) <= max_chars`, both contradicted by `over`). At that point `f.decisions[:n_dec]` is `[]`, `_listing` hits `if not lines: return ""` and returns the empty string *ignoring the `cut` argument*, so the decisions section is dropped together with the `_{decisions_all} more: ddflow decision applicable …_` pointer.

Concretely: a project that sets `[session].agent_brief_max_chars` below the size of the fixed rules text (e.g. `2000` while the rendered `<!-- section: rules -->` block alone is ~2500 chars) with `Facts(decisions=[…3 lines…], decisions_all=3)` gets back `{"decisions_shown": 0, "lessons_shown": 0, "over": True}` and a `text` that contains none of the three decisions that bind the item and no hint that any exist. That directly defeats the stated purpose of the change ("include the current operator decisions that bind the files (D-test-economy-r2, D-review-force-with-reason…)") and defeats the module's own mitigation for trimming decisions — the "N more" note that exists precisely to tell the reader that governing decisions were omitted is removed at the exact moment it is most needed. The pointer should survive even when `n_dec` reaches 0 (e.g. emit the note independently of the listing, or keep it when `decisions_all > 0`).

chunk_findings.detail: The `target` positional is declared unconditionally (`nargs="?"`, `cli_only=True`) but only read on the `--for-agent` branch: `item=a.get("target") or a.get("item") or ""`. On the plain-brief branch the argument goes into the `a` dict and is then thrown away by `item=a.get("item", "")`. Before this change `brief` had no positional, so `ddflow brief P-123` was rejected by the parser ("unrecognized argument") — after this change it parses, the requested item is silently dropped, and the command renders the generic whole-project pack. A coordinator who types the item id positionally (which is exactly the shape advertised for `--for-agent <name> <item>`) gets a plausible-looking brief that is not about that item, with exit status 0 and no warning. The same "accepted but ignored" pattern applies to `--for-agent` combined with `--phase` / `--check-recovery` (swallowed by the `if` branch) and to a bare `--note` (swallowed by the `else` branch), so the command cannot be distinguished from a successful focused run by its output or status.

chunk_findings.detail: The change adds `session.agent_brief_off`, whose documented contract is that a project may name any of `identity, item, decisions, lessons, start, tests, reviews, gates, finish, forbidden, filing, project, report` and have those sections left out of every launch brief. `tests`, `reviews`, `gates`, `forbidden` and `filing` are exactly the ddflow workflow-enforcement text (the gate steps, the test and review commands, the forbidden flags, the filing rule) that `ddflow brief --for-agent` exists to carry. Concretely: with `ddflow config --set session.agent_brief_off '["gates","tests","reviews","forbidden"]'`, `ddflow brief --for-agent alice T1` renders a brief with no gate pipeline, no test command, no review command and no forbidden-flag rule, so a fleet agent launched from it is never told the mandatory workflow at all. That is project configuration *subtracting* ddflow rules, whereas D-rules-hierarchy states that project rules "augment or clarify" while "ddflow rules are hard constraints (e.g., 'must have regression test')" and take precedence; the sibling knob even promises the standard rules can never be trimmed ("the lessons and then the decisions are cut first (the standard rules never are)"), which `agent_brief_off` contradicts by letting them be dropped wholesale. A precedence-preserving design would either keep the enforcement sections non-omittable or make `agent_brief_off` only reorder/de-duplicate them, not remove them.

chunk_findings.detail: The knob is still declared with default `[]` and its contract lets a project name any of `identity, item, decisions, lessons, start, tests, reviews, gates, finish, forbidden, filing, project, report` and have those sections omitted from every launch brief. `tests`, `reviews`, `gates`, `forbidden` and `filing` *are* the ddflow workflow enforcement (the gate steps, the test and review commands, the forbidden flags, the filing rule), which D-rules-hierarchy ranks above project rules and calls a hard constraint. Concrete case: a project config with `session.agent_brief_off = ["gates","tests","forbidden","filing"]` renders every `ddflow brief --for-agent` without the enforcement text, i.e. project configuration overrides ddflow enforcement. The earlier triage for this item says the fix was to *warn in the knob docs* that a section removal drops a standing rule; a documentation note does not implement the precedence — the config still strips the hard constraints, so the violation the previous review reported still holds and the probe does not answer it.

chunk_findings.detail: `agent_brief_off` accepts any subset of `tests, reviews, gates, forbidden, filing` (validated by `_check_brief_sections` against `AGENT_BRIEF_SECTIONS`), so `[session] agent_brief_off = ["gates", "forbidden", "filing"]` produces launch briefs with no gate steps, no forbidden-flag list and no filing rule, while `agent_brief_max_chars` explicitly promises "the standard sections are only ever left out by `agent_brief_off`". The added doc sentence — "only for a project whose own instruction file already says it" — makes the project's rules the authority for removing ddflow enforcement, which is the inverse of D-rules-hierarchy (ddflow workflow enforcement > project rules > agent defaults). The earlier review's fix (docs warning) only re-states the contract; it does not constrain the knob, so the violation of the cited decision is unchanged.

chunk_findings.detail: The knob doc states "Over it, the lessons and then the decisions are cut (down to a pointer)", i.e. lessons are trimmed first and decisions survive longer, but the regression test shipped with this same change (`tests/test_agent_brief.py::test_the_ceiling_cuts_decisions_first_and_never_the_rules`) asserts the opposite order — decisions are cut first. An operator sizing the ceiling around the documented contract (keeping the item's governing decisions, sacrificing lessons) gets the reverse: with a ceiling that fits only one of the two sections, the decisions section is the one reduced to a pointer while the lessons survive, so the brief loses the operator decisions the intent calls out as binding (D-test-economy-r2, D-review-force-with-reason). One of the doc line or the renderer is wrong; as written the knob's stated contract misleads.

chunk_findings.detail: `off` is applied unconditionally to every section name, and neither this module nor its documented contract excludes the ddflow workflow-enforcement sections (`tests`, `reviews`, `gates`, `forbidden`, `filing`) from it: the module docstring states "A section the project switched off (`[session].agent_brief_off`) ... is left out" with no exception, and the loop skips whatever name is present. Given a project config with `agent_brief_off = ["gates", "forbidden"]`, `render(tmpl, f, off={"gates","forbidden"})` drops the gate steps and the forbidden-flag rule from every launch brief, i.e. a project-layer setting silently suppresses the ddflow workflow enforcement text that `ddflow brief --for-agent` exists to deliver. D-rules-hierarchy fixes the ordering as "ddflow workflow enforcement > project rules" and makes those text hard constraints, so a lower-precedence layer must not be able to remove them; the recorded probe ("knob docs now warn it removes a standing rule") only adds a warning to the docs and leaves the behaviour unchanged — a warning does not restore precedence, the section is still omitted from the rendered brief.

chunk_findings.detail: For the launch form the handler refuses `--note` (plain branch) and `--phase` (for-agent branch), per its own contract: *"Flags that belong to the other form are refused rather than ignored."* But `check_recovery` is consumed **only** by the plain branch (`check_recovery=bool(a.get("check_recovery", _api().DEFAULT_CHECK_RECOVERY))`); the `--for-agent` branch never reads it. Given `ddflow brief --for-agent reviewer P-123 --check-recovery`, the flag is accepted into the parsed namespace and then dropped, and the brief is rendered exactly as if it had not been passed — the same silent-ignore failure class the note/phase guards exist to prevent. Under either reading this is wrong: if recovery checking is meaningful to the launch brief it is silently not applied, and if it is not, it should be refused instead of ignored.

chunk_findings.detail: The previous finding still holds: the 6fad6793 change only adds a documentation warning that the knob "removes a standing rule"; it does not stop a project from naming `gates`, `tests`, `reviews`, `forbidden` or `filing` and having the workflow-enforcement text (gate steps, test and review commands, forbidden flags, filing rule) omitted from every launch brief. [D-rules-hierarchy] makes ddflow workflow enforcement a hard constraint that sits *above* project rules ("project rules augment or clarify"), and the example given is exactly "must have regression test". A warning in the docs describes the violation without removing it, so the precedence is still project-config-over-ddfllow. Demonstrated input: a project config with `session.agent_brief_off = ["gates", "tests", "reviews", "forbidden", "filing"]` → every `brief --for-agent` now omits the gate steps, the test/review commands and the forbidden flags, and the regression-test constraint is no longer delivered to agents.

chunk_findings.detail: The earlier review's finding #3 is marked `confirmed` and triaged as fixed, but the "fix" described is only a documentation warning ("knob docs now warn it removes a standing rule"); the knob's contract is unchanged and still lets a project name any of `tests`, `reviews`, `gates`, `forbidden`, `filing` — which is exactly the ddflow workflow-enforcement text (gate steps, test/review commands, forbidden flags, filing rule) — and have those sections left out of every launch brief. Concretely, with project config `session.agent_brief_off = ["gates", "forbidden", "filing"]` (default is `[]` only until someone sets it), the rendered brief for any item silently omits the gate steps, the forbidden-flag list and the filing rule, i.e. a project-level setting overrides a ddflow hard constraint. `D-rules-hierarchy` states the precedence explicitly: "ddflow workflow enforcement > project rules > agent defaults … ddflow rules are hard constraints (e.g., 'must have regression test')", and a warning in the knob's docs neither prevents that override nor restores the precedence — it only informs the operator that they are doing it. So the violation still holds and the documentation change does not answer it; the knob should not be able to disable the enforcement sections, or the precedence decision needs to be amended before this is a valid fix.

chunk_findings.detail: The new knob lets a project point `prompts.agent_brief` at a template that "replac[es] the shipped one", and that template is rendered for every `ddflow brief --for-agent` launch. The shipped template is precisely where the ddflow workflow-enforcement text lives — the gate steps (`ddflow gate status`, the `failed`/`unavailable` rule, the regression-test rule), the `ddflow tests`/`ddflow review` commands, the `Never` list (push/stash/force/secrets/foreign leases) and the filing rule — so a project-level file can silently delete hard constraints from every agent brief, with nothing in the change requiring a replacement to retain them. This is the same hazard that was already confirmed and fixed for the sibling knob `session.agent_brief_off` in this item (the fix added a warning that switching a section off removes a standing rule), yet this upgrade entry ships with only `why = "Path to a launch-brief template replacing the shipped one."` and no equivalent warning. Concretely: a project adds `prompts.agent_brief = "docs/brief.md"` whose body is just the item heading and globs; every agent launched afterwards gets no gate, test, review, forbidden-flag or filing instructions, and neither the upgrade note nor the knob docs tell the operator that ddflow enforcement was dropped. That inverts the precedence in [D-rules-hierarchy] ("ddflow rules are hard constraints; project rules augment or clarify").

chunk_findings.detail: The documented contract of the new knob lets a project name any of `tests, reviews, gates, forbidden, filing` and have those sections "left out of every launch brief". Those five sections are precisely the ddflow workflow-enforcement text (gate steps, test and review commands, forbidden flags, filing rule) that `ddflow brief --for-agent` exists to distribute. [D-rules-hierarchy] says precedence is "ddflow workflow enforcement > project rules > agent defaults" and that "ddflow rules are hard constraints", i.e. a project's own config/rules may augment or clarify but may not take a ddflow-enforced rule away. With `session.agent_brief_off = ["tests","reviews","gates","forbidden","filing"]` in project config, every rendered launch brief silently loses exactly those hard constraints — project config overriding ddflow enforcement. The previous triage ("knob docs now warn it removes a standing rule") does not answer the rule: the added sentence "only for a project whose own instruction file already says it" is documentation only; it changes no precedence, no validation, and no rendering behaviour, so the violation still holds. That the operator asked for sections to be switchable is not a waiver of the hierarchy either — the switchable set is not restricted to non-enforcement sections (identity/item/finish/project/report), and nothing in the code or config schema blocks the enforcement ones. Either the enforcement sections must be non-removable, or the knob's set must exclude them.

chunk_findings.detail: The earlier finding that `session.agent_brief_off` lets project config strip the ddflow workflow-enforcement sections still holds, and the triage's "fix" (a warning sentence in the knob docs plus `default off=[]`) does not answer it. [D-rules-hierarchy] states the precedence order is `ddflow workflow enforcement > project rules > agent defaults`, with ddflow rules being hard constraints. `forbidden` (the forbidden-flag list), `filing` (the filing rule), and also `tests`, `reviews`, `gates` are precisely that enforcement text, and this change's own test locks in the ability to remove them: `run_cli(proj, "config", "session.agent_brief_off", "filing,forbidden")` followed by `assert "filing" not in sections and "forbidden" not in sections` — i.e. a project-level setting is asserted to override ddflow rules, which the hierarchy forbids. Documentation of a violation is not a guard against it: given a project with `session.agent_brief_off = "gates,tests,reviews,forbidden,filing"`, every `--for-agent` brief silently omits the gate steps, test/review commands and forbidden flags, which is the exact cross-agent rule drift the command was introduced to eliminate (the intent says the standard text must come from one place and carry "the current operator decisions that bind the files"). A config write is the only input needed to reproduce it; the added warning text changes nothing about the output.

chunk_findings.detail: The change still exposes `session.agent_brief_off`, a project-settable list that may name any of `identity, item, decisions, lessons, start, tests, reviews, gates, finish, forbidden, filing, project, report`, and have those sections omitted from *every* launch brief — including `tests`, `reviews`, `gates`, `forbidden` and `filing`, i.e. exactly the ddflow workflow-enforcement text (gate steps, test/review commands, forbidden flags, filing rule). The previous review raised this under [D-rules-hierarchy], and the triage says it was fixed in 6fad6793 by adding a warning to the knob's documentation. That fix does not answer the objection: [D-rules-hierarchy] states that precedence is ddflow workflow enforcement > project rules, and that ddflow rules are *hard constraints* (e.g. "must have regression test"). A doc warning leaves the mechanism intact — a project's `.ddflow` config (project rules, the lower tier) can still delete the ddflow-enforcement sections from the brief for all its agents, so the hard-constraint tier is still overridable by the tier below it. The default `[]` is irrelevant to this: the demonstrating input is a project config setting `session.agent_brief_off = ["gates", "tests", "reviews", "forbidden", "filing"]`, after which `ddflow brief --for-agent` emits a brief that never tells the agent the gate pipeline, the test/review commands, the forbidden flags or the filing rule, in violation of the stated precedence. Either those sections must be non-suppressible (only advisory sections such as `decisions`/`lessons`/`project` removable), or the knob cannot live at the project/rules tier.

chunk_findings.detail: The triage for the earlier finding #3 claims it is answered because the knob docs "now warn it removes a standing rule", but that is a documentation-only change: the behaviour is untouched. The knob's contract is still that a *project* (file/CLI/MCP/prompt config) may name any of `tests, reviews, gates, forbidden, filing, project` and have those sections omitted from every launch brief. Those sections are exactly the ddflow workflow-enforcement text (gate steps, test and review commands, forbidden flags, filing rule). `D-rules-hierarchy` states the precedence explicitly: "ddflow workflow enforcement > project rules > agent defaults", and that "ddflow rules are hard constraints (e.g., 'must have regression test')". A project-level setting that can delete the enforcement section from a fleet agent's only launch document inverts that precedence — the project config wins over the hard constraint. Concretely: `agent_brief_off = ["tests","gates","forbidden"]` in a project's config renders a brief whose `## tests`, `## gates` and forbidden-flag text are gone (the `_listing`/section-skip path returns the section as empty), so an agent launched from it never sees the regression-test requirement or the forbidden flags, while the system still reports the brief as valid. A caution paragraph in the knob's docs does not stop that config from being set, so the confirmed finding still holds; the fix needs either a hard-coded non-disableable core (the D-rules-hierarchy enforcement sections) or an operator-level (not project-level) override.
chunk_findings.title: session.agent_brief_off (section filter used by `ddflow brief --for-agent`) [D-rules-hierarchy]

chunk_findings.detail: `agent_brief_off` lets a project remove `gates`, `forbidden` and `filing` from every launch brief — sections that carry ddflow workflow enforcement (the gate steps and the forbidden-flag/pin rules the brief exists to standardize). With a project config containing `[session].agent_brief_off = ["gates", "forbidden"]`, every `ddflow brief --for-agent` render for that project drops the gate steps and the forbidden-flag rules, so the subagent never sees the ddflow-mandated gates. That is project configuration overriding ddflow workflow enforcement, which D-rules-hierarchy says must take precedence ("ddflow workflow enforcement > project rules > agent defaults; ddflow rules are hard constraints"). The docstring's hedge ("only for a project whose own instruction file already says it") is a usage note, not an enforced guard: nothing in the knob or its `_check_brief_sections` check distinguishes a project-local convention section (`project`, `lessons`) from a ddflow hard-constraint section, so all thirteen can be switched off with equal ease.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/config_sections/session.py `agent_brief_off` (and its docstring)

chunk_findings.detail: The change carries the standard agent rules — the module docstring lists them as "identity, claim and worktree steps, merge-main-first, pins, the test economy, review and gate rules, merge and complete, forbidden actions, the filing rule" — in a Markdown prompt template (`templates/prompts/agent_brief.md`, override `[prompts].agent_brief`) whose structure is a bespoke `<!-- section: NAME -->` grammar parsed by `SECTION = re.compile(r"^<!--\s*section:\s*([a-z_]+)\s*-->")`. Sections carry no `id`/`title`/`tags`/`scope`/`priority` frontmatter, so these binding rules are not expressed in the project's rule format. [D-rules-format] requires rules to be TOML with a frontmatter block (id, title, tags, scope, priority) + body, precisely so they stay config-familiar and machine-resolvable. Concretely: to add or re-scope a rule (e.g. a new forbidden flag, or restricting the test-economy rule to certain paths) an author must hand-edit an un-numbered/un-scoped Markdown section rather than write a TOML rule record that `ddflow rule list` / `ddflow decision applicable <item>` can enumerate, order by priority, or scope to files; nothing in this file (or the template it renders) gives the rules ids, scopes, or priorities, so the precedence machinery of the rule system cannot see them. The change therefore introduces the "alternative" format that [D-rules-format] rejected.

chunk_findings.detail: The module docstring states the contract explicitly: "Flags that belong to the other form are refused rather than ignored: a brief that quietly is not about the item asked for is worse than none." The code enforces this only partially. `--phase` (session-pack only) is refused in the `--for-agent` branch, and `--note` (agent-only) is refused in the session branch, but `check_recovery` — read from the same parsed args `a` and passed to `_api().brief(...)` only in the session branch — is never refused in the `--for-agent` branch and never reaches `_api().agent_brief`. Concretely, `ddflow brief --for-agent w1 D-x --check-recovery` (or the same invocation with `--check-recovery` supplied by a wrapper/config-merged arg dict) returns a successful launch brief and silently drops the flag the operator supplied, which is exactly the "quietly is not about the item asked for" failure mode the docstring says the code avoids. Either refuse it alongside `--phase`, or document that session-only knobs are ignored for the agent form.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/declared/agent_brief_cli.py:call

chunk_findings.detail: The change adds a CLI positional `target` to `brief`, but its own `cli_help` scopes it to the new agent path ("with --for-agent: the item id") and the pre-existing item plumbing (`item=a.get("item", "")`) is unchanged, so `target` is only consumed when `--for-agent` is given. The CLI now accepts a bare id on the default path: `ddflow brief D-test-economy-r2` parses `D-test-economy-r2` into `target` (not `item`), reaches `AB.call` with `for_agent=""`, and renders the generic, unfocused brief with exit 0. Before this change that same invocation was rejected by the argument parser ("unrecognized arguments"), so the failure is now silent: the user gets a different brief than the one requested and no diagnostic. Either the positional must be folded into `item` for the non-agent path (and its help/cli_help widened accordingly), or the positional should not be declared on the plain path at all.

chunk_findings.detail: The identity section states the emission rule — "Pass `--agent {{ agent }}` on every ddflow CLI call (MCP: `as_agent`), so claims, gates and reviews are attributed to you" — but no command that the rendered brief actually tells the agent to run carries that flag. Given agent `foo` and item `X`, the rendered Start section reads `1. \`ddflow brief --item X\`, then \`ddflow claim X\``; step 2 renders `ddflow update X --globs ...` and `ddflow heartbeat X`; the Tests section `ddflow tests --item X`; Reviews `ddflow review X --gate <gate>` / `ddflow review show X --gate <gate>`; Gates `ddflow gate status X`; Finish `ddflow merge X --model ...` / `ddflow complete X --model ...`; Filing `ddflow bug found` / `ddflow task add ...`. An agent that copies these commands literally performs an unattributed claim and review round, which is precisely the "drift between launches" this feature (P-agent-parity.launcher) exists to eliminate — the general prose sentence is the only place the flag survives, and the stated regression test ("the rendered brief contains … the agent flag") passes on that prose even though the executable instructions are unattributed. Step 1 is the sharpest instance: it re-invokes `ddflow brief --item {{ item }}` with neither `--agent` nor the `--for-agent <name>` form the intent documents for selecting the agent, so the one command whose whole purpose is agent selection cannot select the agent it is addressed to.

chunk_findings.detail: The test blesses a brief that no longer carries the mandatory standard text. Under either reading this is wrong: if recovery checking is meaningful to the launch brief it is silently not applied, and if it is not, it should be refused instead of ignored.

Given a project that supplies its own `.ddflow/prompts/agent_brief.md` containing an additional section, e.g. `<!-- section: security -->`, the natural way to switch that standing block off in config — `[session] agent_brief_off = ["security"]` — is rejected at config load with `unknown section(s) ['security']; known: identity, item, ...`, even though the section does render in every brief for that project. chunk_findings.detail: The rendered brief still never shows a command carrying the flag it insists on. The identity line states the rule — "Pass `--agent {{ agent }}` on every ddflow CLI call (MCP: `as_agent`), so claims, gates and reviews are attributed to you" — but every command the brief actually prints to the agent is flagless: `ddflow claim {{ item }}` (line 24), `ddflow update {{ item }} --globs "..."` / `ddflow heartbeat {{ item }}` (line 25), `ddflow tests --item {{ item }}`, `ddflow review {{ item }} --gate <gate>` / `ddflow review show {{ item }} --gate <gate>`, `ddflow gate status {{ item }}`, `ddflow merge {{ item }} --model <your model family>` / `ddflow complete {{ item }} --model <your model family>`. Concretely, with agent `foo` and item `T1`, an agent that runs the steps as written executes `ddflow claim T1` and `ddflow review T1 --gate gate1` with no `--agent foo`, so the claim, heartbeat and gate/review records are not attributed to `foo` — exactly the failure the identity sentence says the flag prevents, and the brief is a numbered checklist that invites literal copying. This is not answered by the probe recorded for the earlier refutation: that probe only shows that `ddflow complete` still enforces the *gate* sections at completion time (exit 3 "required gate(s) not passed"), i.e. it covers `gates`/`forbidden`/`filing`, which have a tool-time backstop. chunk_findings.detail:
`commits` is built as `", ".join(ld["commits"])` **plus** the `" (+N more)"` suffix, and the caller then uses `if commits:` (line 74) to decide whether to print `; commits {commits}`. Because the suffix is concatenated before the truthiness test, `commits` is non-empty even when there are zero shas to show, so the guard no longer asks "are there commit shas?".

Concrete input: `d["landing"] = {"commits": [], "commits_total": 3, "merge_sha": "0123456789ab...", "base": "main", "branch_head": None, "completed_at": None, ...}`. Then `", ".join([])` is `""`, the condition `3 > 0` holds, so `commits == " (+3 more)"`; line 74 is true and `landing` becomes

    merged 0123456789ab into main; commits  (+3 more)

i.e. the commit shas the intent requires ("merge/commit shas") are silently absent, the suffix is attached to nothing (note the double space after `commits`), and the reader is told there are "3 more" commits while none are listed. The collector can produce this shape whenever `commits_total` counts commits that the `commits` list itself omitted (e.g. merge-only branch, or a filtered/capped list); the fix is to keep the shas and the suffix separate and test the shas list, not the concatenated string.

chunk_findings.detail: The new command is deliberately made CLI-only: `tool=""` with the reason "a `tools/list` is within a few bytes of its budget; an MCP agent reads the same facts through `ddflow_show` and `ddflow_gate_status`". In the same change `agent_brief.md` now unconditionally instructs an agent to "End your run with ONLY the output of `ddflow report {{ item }} --agent {{ agent }}`" — i.e. to run a command that, by construction, has no MCP tool. The project explicitly supports agents that consume the MCP surface (that is why the reason names `ddflow_show`/`ddflow_gate_status` as their substitute); such an agent cannot invoke `ddflow report`, and the previous manual report (which an MCP agent *could* assemble from `ddflow_show`/`ddflow_gate_status`) has been deleted from the brief. The result is that for any MCP-only run the operator gets no report at all, and the overrides/skips/caveats this change exists to preserve are exactly what is lost. Either the brief needs an MCP fallback path or the tool cannot be CLI-only.

chunk_findings.detail: The new sentence orders the actions as "run `ddflow report {{ item }} --agent {{ agent }}` anyway and file that as a task or bug". `report` renders its `filed` / `follow_ups` / `not_done` sections from the log at the moment it runs. An agent that follows the written order — produce the report, then record the caveat as a task/bug — emits a report whose `filed`/`follow_ups` sections do not contain that task/bug, and the brief forbids any prose after the report, so the caveat (the very thing this change claims to stop forgetting) never reaches the operator. The instruction needs to file the task/bug *before* generating the report.
